name: Familiarity Stability Control
selection_rationale: High novelty and falsifiability with direct relevance to FRANK's mandatory user-adaptive Retina path: treat familiarity learning as a closed-loop controller over a frozen representation, with explicit admission, uncertainty and rollback state rather than unconstrained self-training.
primary_hypothesis: For FRANK v0.1, a frozen visual backbone plus prototype/linear readout can safely lower recurring visual compute only if online updates are controlled by evidence-tier admission and open-set feedback. BRONZE self-predictions must not directly update trusted prototypes/classifier state because the resulting positive feedback loop can degrade unknown rejection and eventually known-class performance under sustained OOD contamination.
counterhypotheses: A sufficiently conservative confidence threshold on self-training alone is enough; provenance-tier admission adds complexity without measurable robustness gain.
Prototype-only learning is too weak under user-specific drift; a continually adapted backbone is required despite added forgetting risk.
Unknown rejection should be handled entirely by downstream Retina, so the micro-classifier does not need an explicit open-set controller.
falsifier_or_completion_test: On frozen user-specific replay plus injected near-OOD streams, compare naive confident self-update against GOLD/SILVER-gated updates. The field hypothesis is weakened if naive self-update matches or beats gated updates on known retention, false-familiarity/open-set rejection, calibration and compute cost across contamination levels without rollback intervention.

external_evidence.finding: continual test-time self-training can accumulate pseudo-label errors and catastrophically forget under non-stationary shifts
continual entropy-minimization adaptation can collapse; stability constraints materially matter
reusing incorrect predictions can cause long-horizon degradation and creates an attack surface
open-world test-time training benefits from explicit strong-OOD filtering and dynamic prototype handling

findings: Synthetic 2D frozen-embedding simulation supports the direction, not a FRANK-specific claim: naive self-update admitted increasing fractions of unknown samples as contamination rose.
At 40% unknown contamination, naive unknown rejection averaged about 0.319 versus about 0.419 for trust-gated updates while known accuracy stayed about 0.999-1.000.
At 70% unknown contamination, about 72.4% of naive accepted updates were actually unknown; known accuracy dropped to about 0.987 while trust-gated remained about 1.000 in this synthetic setup.
The most important control variable is not classifier confidence alone but evidence admission authority: prediction confidence must not be allowed to bootstrap itself into training truth.

ClayCode BASE therefore needs explicit representability for learner version, evidence tier, candidate/current state, open-set result, promotion/rejection and rollback receipts; this is already directionally required by the owner-fixed visual learning directive and does not yet justify new language semantics.
next_test: Run MVC-E4/MVC-E5 in H1 with real frozen Retina embeddings and user-specific replay; sweep contamination, confidence thresholds and GOLD/SILVER support requirements, then compare prototypes vs linear head under identical resource budgets.
